messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered (service=redis-accept-queue) at 2026-03-10T14:20:01Z — threshold: accept_queue_depth > 200 for 3m
Amy (oncall): Acked via PagerDuty. I'll take first look. Paging Chris for possible capacity.
Chris (sre): on it. seeing a spike in accepted connections and a ton of TIME_WAIT sockets to redis nodes. throwing up quick metrics: accepted_connections_rate +400% over 1m, rejected_connections since 14:18: ~270, avg latency 120ms -> 2s tail.
Amy (oncall): Customers: a subset of write-heavy customers are seeing 502s and high tail latency. Dave in support flagged 18 reports in 15 mins. Putting ETA: 30m for mitigation.
Chris (sre): running quick checks — ssh to redis-01: `redis-cli -h redis-01 INFO clients | egrep "connected_clients|maxclients"` output:
```
connected_clients:1023
maxclients:1024
rejected_connections:273
```
Also: `redis-cli -h redis-01 CLIENT LIST | wc -l` -> 1005 (close to connected_clients)
Amy (oncall): @Paul can we scale read-replicas or add capacity to the cluster? Are we on autoscale?
Paul (infra): Autoscale is per-workload and we are at max desired for that pool. I can spin up a temporary warm node group and add it to service routing, will take ~6m to provision + join. Meanwhile we should reduce connection pressure.
Maria (eng): Noted a surge from a batch job retry loop from service-x — looks like a client reconnect loop. I'm putting a kill switch on that job (deploying a patch to stop aggressive reconnects).
Chris (sre): Short-term mitigation: enabling connection-limits at proxy layer to shed excess new connections and apply 429s back to clients. Pushing rate-limit rule now to edge-proxy.
Amy (oncall): Applying proxy rule: `edge-proxyctl apply --rule "redis-client-connection-rate-limit=50/s per-ip"` — applying now.
Chris (sre): Rule active. New connection rate dropping. Rejected_connections rate trending down from 25/s to 5/s. Redis accepted connections stabilizing around 650.
Paul (infra): New extra node group built and added to pool, redis-svc rebalanced shards to include redis-04. Took longer due to warmup, but online.
Amy (oncall): Re-checking client errors: 502s dropped from 8.7% -> 1.2% over last 5m. Support: @Dave please update customers with mitigations and expected follow-up.
Dave (support): Sending note now. Marking affected customers list and asking for logs from service-x to confirm they stopped retries.
Maria (eng): patch deployed to service-x to add exponential backoff + socket reuse. Also code now logs connection errors; rolling to 100% in 2m.
Chris (sre): Post-mitigation stats: connected_clients 540, maxclients 1024, rejected_connections steady at ~2/min, p95 latency back to 60ms. No new spikes for 8m.
Amy (oncall): Handing back to SRE on-call for monitoring. I'll stay on the thread for 30m watch. @Chris please confirm stable for handback.
Chris (sre): Confirmed stable. Leaving monitoring dashboard open; will create an incident ticket and follow-up runbook item to prevent client-side retry loops.
Amy (oncall): Closing PagerDuty incident (resolved) and leaving follow-up actions in #postmortems. Thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident resolved by Amy at 2026-03-10T14:40:50Z (duration 20m 49s) — incident id PAG-738291
Maria (eng): I'll own a follow-up PR to instrument client pools and add connection reuse guidance. Assigning to me and tagging infra.
Paul (infra): I'll add capacity guardrails to autoscale policy and a pre-warm step for spikes. Filing infra task.
Amy (oncall): Summary for postmortem: root cause likely aggressive retry loop from service-x causing connection pileup; mitigations: proxy rate-limit, temporary capacity increase, fix client behavior. Next steps: postmortem + alert tuning (lower noise, add upstream client error metric).
